bull_bear.body: 100% internal funding; no debt raised; dividend payout of ₹5/share (250% of face value) maintained despite capex; no buyback announced; retained earnings fully deployed into capex and tree farming initiatives.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Duty-free paper imports (up 68% YoY, China +181%, ASEAN +247%); wood scarcity and price volatility; delayed NCLAT clearance for Servalakshmi acquisition; prolonged margin pressure until H2FY25; lack of BIS/QCO enforcement on imported paper.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges severe headwinds but emphasizes operational resilience, strategic capex, and ESG leadership; strong emphasis on lobbying for import duties and land access for plantations; confident in long-term growth despite short-term pain.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Company plants 115 crore seedlings over 7 years — equivalent to 1.3 lakh acres — creating a de facto raw material monopoly via contract farming; this vertical integration is more strategic than any capacity expansion; also, 90% of wood is sourced from 5 lakh farmers — making SPB a rural employment engine, not just a paper maker.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Product diversification / depth across paper grades lets the company retune product-mix to counter cheaper imports and shifting demand, credited for a resilient domestic sales performance despite intense import competition
- Flexibility and agility in adapting product mix to dynamic market conditions, evidenced by highest-ever annual domestic sales (2,28,955 tonnes) in FY26 despite challenging conditions
- Conversion-capacity upgrade (new sheeter at Erode) enabling supply of high-realisation copier products to the US market, supporting a rebound in exports in Q4FY26
- Stable industrial relations — the 10th five-year wage settlement for the Erode unit was concluded during FY26, valid through 31.03.2029, giving multi-year labour-cost certainty
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Import pressure and trade-policy risk — Surging cheap paper imports from ASEAN and China (ASEAN imports up ~250% and Chinese imports up ~181% over two years) enter largely duty-free under AIFTA, at an estimated USD 40-50/tonne versus India's ~USD 110/tonne cost of production — a gap domestic producers cannot bridge without trade protection; only a temporary MIP on VPB has been imposed so far and broader safeguard duties are still being sought by the industry.
- Wood fibre scarcity and cost escalation — Wood availability in Tamil Nadu/South India is acutely tight, with Casuarina and Eucalyptus prices escalating due to competition from plywood, MDF and particle-board industries and new pulp mill capacities; the company's own SWOT also flags a large government-owned competitor in the same state competing aggressively for wood sourcing.
- Currency risk raising imported input costs — Steep INR depreciation over the last five years benefits exports but raises the cost of imported coal, chemicals and market pulp, an integrated-mill input-cost exposure.
- Climate and water risk — Erratic monsoons and reduced water flows in the River Cauvery are flagged as a structural concern for the company's Tamil Nadu-based mills.
- Structural digitisation pressure on Printing & Writing paper — Newsprint and the P&W segment face secular decline from digital media, e-invoicing and digital documentation, only partly offset by education-sector demand; the pace is slower in India than mature markets but the headwind is structural.
- Import dependency for key inputs at Unit II/III — Company's own SWOT flags dependency on imported pulp / waste-paper for Unit-II/III and on imported coal, plus non-availability of indigenous coal — exposing operating costs to global commodity and freight cycles.
- Export-market concentration and trade-policy exposure — The US is the company's major export market; US tariff-related disruptions suspended exports there from May'25-Sep'25 in FY26, forcing volumes into an already import-pressured domestic market — illustrating the concentration risk even though stability has since been restored.
- Scale and vintage disadvantage versus larger/global players — Company's own SWOT cites lack of size and multiple machines as a high-cost disadvantage, and older machines/buildings, versus the scale and cost advantages the industry associates with larger integrated producers.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Erode unit produced 1.65 lakh tonnes (highest ever), contributing ~69% of total production; Fine Paper segment to be expanded via Servalakshmi acquisition (75,000 tonnes pa); Writing & Printing grades dominate revenue but face pricing pressure; pulp self-sufficiency remains core strategic focus.

business.body: Seshasayee Paper and Boards manufactures paper — chiefly printing & writing / copier grades — and wet lap pulp at two units in Tamil Nadu, Erode and Tirunelveli, selling to domestic and export markets (with the US a key export destination). The company also undertakes limited trading activity in petroleum products and note books alongside its core paper business.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin compressed due to 40-50% wood cost inflation (Tamil Nadu-specific); realisation down 15-20% YoY on W&P grades due to Chinese/ASEAN imports; cost recovery expected only if import duties are imposed or wood supply stabilizes.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Expecting challenging market conditions for W&P grades until Q2FY25, with recovery anticipated in H2FY25; full-year FY25 PAT guidance not provided, but management expects improved performance post-capacity augmentation and import duty intervention.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 20% capacity augmentation at Erode unit (pending environment clearance); integration of Servalakshmi unit (75ktpa fine paper) by FY26; potential for export market penetration if import duties are imposed; agro-forestry expansion to secure 100% wood supply.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Product diversification strategy: retune product-mix flexibly and with agility to counter cheaper imports and dynamic market conditions, credited for the company's resilient domestic sales performance
- Upgrade conversion capacity toward high-realisation grades — commissioning of an additional sheeter at Erode to supply high-realisation copier products to the US market
- Continued cost reduction / optimisation efforts to defend operating margins against realisation pressure
- Continue tree farming activity to support quality wood/fibre supply (raw-material security), per Board's Report reference to ongoing tree farming programme
- The Board follows a Dividend Distribution Policy adopted under SEBI (LODR) Regulation 43A, published on the company's website, under which a per-share dividend is recommended annually to shareholders.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The company completed Mill Development Plan-III (MDP-III) at Unit: Erode in phases during FY2020-21 and FY2021-22, which augmented Erode's annual installed paper capacity to 1,65,000 tonnes; Unit: Tirunelveli's installed capacity remains unchanged at 90,000 tonnes, taking total installed capacity to 2,55,000 tonnes per annum. During FY26 the company successfully commissioned an additional sheeter at Unit: Erode, augmenting conversion capacity to supply high-realisation copier products to the US market. No new capacity-expansion project (beyond the completed MDP-III and the FY26 sheeter) is described in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Domestic packaging boards (corrugated, carton board, duplex) growing 8-9% p.a., driven by e-commerce, food delivery and organised retail
- Printing & Writing segment stabilising after years of digitisation pressure, with NEP 2020-driven school enrollment providing a partial offset
- Tissue and hygiene paper growing 7-8% as middle-class penetration deepens
- Newsprint in secular decline at (-)4-5% p.a.
- Cheaper duty-free imports from China and Indonesia remain the industry's biggest pain point; GST 2.0 reforms (Sep'25) with NIL GST on notebook paper temporarily gave imported paper a 12-15% cost advantage over domestic production, before market prices settled in Q4 at levels below pre-reform prices
- US tariff-related disruption suspended exports to the US from May'25-Sep'25, forcing extra volumes into an already import-pressured domestic market and steepening the realisation decline; post the US Supreme Court's tariff decision, stability has been restored to export volumes and the outlook for this segment is favourable
- Global supply-chain volatility — escalation of the US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption in early 2026 — has raised the cost of imported pulp, waste paper, chemicals and coal, expected to significantly affect margins in H1FY27
- International paper prices from Indonesia and China remain weak with no signs of recovery
- FY27 industry consensus is for a 6-7% CAGR in paper consumption, led by packaging/paperboard (e-commerce, FMCG, quick-commerce) and with printing & writing paper gaining traction from NEP 2020 implementation and rising textbook/competitive-exam volumes; tissue & hygiene paper expected to grow at double-digit rates
- FY27 expected to be a watershed year for sustainable packaging adoption — phased EPR norm rollout, brand plastic-substitution mandates and demand for FSC-certified/food-grade/recyclable paperboard reshaping product mix, with specialty papers (release liners, thermal, decor, filter, food-service grades) seeing double-digit growth and higher realisations for mills with R&D, certifications and downstream relationships
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Despite severe market headwinds from duty-free paper imports and elevated wood costs, Seshasayee delivered resilient FY24 performance with record production and nil net debt, positioning itself for growth via strategic asset acquisition and 20% capacity expansion in Erode, though near-term margins remain pressured until FY25 recovery.

open.item: Following the US Supreme Court's decision on US tariffs, stability has been restored to the company's export volumes to the US, and the outlook for this export segment is stated to be favourable.
Board recommended a dividend of Rs 2.00 per equity share (face value Rs 2), absorbing Rs 12.61 crores, payable to shareholders on the register as of 10.06.2026.

Global supply-chain volatility from the US-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption has significantly increased the cost of imported pulp, waste paper, chemicals and coal, which management expects to significantly affect margins in the first half of FY27.

Consensus view per management's outlook is that operating margins will continue the recovery that began in FY26, as FY27 is expected to be a year of recovery and reset for the Indian paper industry — provided policy support holds and global pulp markets stabilise as expected.
